convention: All exponential times are amplitude-envelope e-folding times. Oscillator tau_amp=2Q/omega0=Q/(pi*f0); energy decay is half as long. Propagation windows are stored separately.
hypothetical_receiver_default: 1 MHz first-order envelope pole after carrier conversion, tau=1/(2*pi*1e6). Explicitly authorised by the user where source timing is absent; not a published detector specification.
use: These are component-level response benchmarks. They do not add a second response factor to input-referred noise PSDs. Finite-duration reach requires a finite-waveform/noise integral and an observation window.

adv_ligo.name: LIGO HF (analytic)

components.name: comb_tooth
components.scope: Representative optical comb tooth with assumed power FWHM 1 kHz. The physical FSR is c/(2L), not the legacy 1000 Hz ASD anchor.

assumptions: Loaded FWHM of 1 kHz is an explicit hypothetical representative tooth. Real linewidth and response vary with tooth/frequency; the plotted smooth ASD does not specify them.
For duration diagnostics, apply the same assumed 1 kHz linewidth to each notional comb tooth; this is not a reconstructed frequency-dependent optical comb.
limitations: The smooth analytic ASD remains a sensitivity envelope, not the reconstructed resonant optical comb. A single component time is not a validated high-frequency GW response.

mago_broad.name: MAGO (broadband)

components.name: mechanical_mode
components.scope: Approximate lowest mechanical mode benchmark. Only relevant near the mechanical mode.

components.name: signal_em_mode
components.scope: Broadband loaded signal EM mode benchmark, Sec. V and App. G. Q_loaded, not intrinsic Q=1e10; pump is already filled. GW drive centre is the mode splitting omega_1-omega_pump, approximately 1e4 rad/s, not the GHz carrier.

assumptions: Use the order-of-magnitude angular-frequency benchmarks as written in the source (rad/s); exact geometry/mode values of the digitised curve are not supplied.
limitations: Coupled mechanical/EM response, detuning, and pump dynamics are not fully reconstructed. Appendix F.2 has a dimensionally inverted printed ring-up expression; times are derived from the damped equations.
